public_rationale: Actual institutional reductions establish the limited budget-cut condition. National funding data show pressure but also important variation. Neither source measures how many universities can afford the proposed replacement. No decisive event meets the early-resolution rule, and Marcus gives no deadline. Non-adoption cannot be counted as financial inability.
limitations: US universities are an interpretive population choice.
Public-sector funding data do not cover every university or every source of instructional funding.
Institutional cuts do not establish sector-wide inability.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: With university budgets being cut, few universities will have enough money to replace term papers with small TA-led sections.

statement.excerpt: With enough money you can have TAs and smaller sections of say 20 students each, taught by teaching assistants, but with university budgets being slashed, few universities will have enough money to make that work.
statement.document_title: ”Everyone is cheating their way through college” with GenAI. Who should bear the costs?

from_speaker: few universities will have enough money
smaller sections of say 20 students each
our_interpretation: The forecast concerns the financial capacity to replace term-paper functions with roughly 20-student TA-led sections across affected large courses.
Actual adoption is not equivalent to affordability: universities may choose other assessment methods.
Few means a small minority, without imposing a numerical cutoff Marcus did not provide.
I use US universities as the principal population given the surrounding discussion of university funding cuts, while flagging the unspecified geography.
The condition is that universities face actual budget reductions, not that every university's budget falls. The cited institutional reductions establish that limited antecedent.
criteria.support_condition: While the budget-cut condition holds, representative institutional budgets and staffing-cost estimates show that only a small minority can sustainably fund the proposed replacement at the required scale.
criteria.contradiction_condition: While the condition holds, representative evidence shows that a substantial share clearly exceeding a small minority can sustainably fund the proposed replacement.

evidence.explanation: The university links implemented management reductions to budget cuts and rising labor costs. This establishes actual institutional retrenchment, but neither its national prevalence nor inability to fund TA sections.

evidence.publisher: State Higher Education Executive Officers Association
evidence.explanation: The report shows lower funding per student alongside increased aggregate inflation-adjusted appropriations. That mixed funding picture does not establish widespread severe budget cuts or the share able to afford the proposed sections.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: A representative, costed assessment of universities' capacity to provide roughly 20-student TA-led replacements under actual budget cuts, or broad funded implementation clearly inconsistent with only a small minority being able to afford them.
